subject.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a narrowed pre-auth observation hook while requiring sender grouping and `/allowlist` ergonomics to extend the existing generic `accessGroups` contract?
rationale: The workflow has strong proof, but automation cannot choose whether blocked content should enter a permanent hook API or whether OpenClaw should maintain two overlapping access-group models.

options.title: Narrow and converge
options.body: Keep the generic pre-auth seam, remove the fixed six-value taxonomy, and extend canonical access groups only where sender classification is demonstrably needed.

options.title: Approve distinct sender roles
options.body: Retain the fixed role taxonomy only after defining distinct naming, authorization semantics, migration behavior, and compatibility tests that separate it from generic access groups.

options.title: Decline core adoption
options.body: Keep access-request notification in managed external hooks or security-audit tooling without adding these permanent plugin and config contracts.

recommendation.title: Narrow and converge
recommendation.body: Keep the generic pre-auth seam, remove the fixed six-value taxonomy, and extend canonical access groups only where sender classification is demonstrably needed.

likelyOwner.reason: His merged work most directly owns the shared authorization and plugin SDK boundary that must remain canonical.
